sources_considered.why: Read the original theoretical paper. It addresses unavoidable errors under a formal definition, but does not establish commercial or technological futility.
Read as a theoretical cross-check. Its calibration and arbitrary-fact assumptions likewise do not establish a general barrier to useful applications.
Read the original field-study paper for evidence of useful deployment despite model limitations.
Read the deployment section to establish that most adoption occurred during November 2020 through February 2021.

receipt.public_excerpt: impossible to eliminate hallucination in LLMs.

evidence_items.explanation: The proof concerns disagreement between computable models and ground-truth functions over a general problem space. It supports a limitation on universal correctness, but does not show that useful, sufficiently reliable applications cannot improve.

The field study documents useful customer-support assistance, challenging an inference from hallucinations to general uselessness. It studies human-assisted work and does not establish autonomous reliability or continued progress beyond the post.

unresolved_gaps: The theoretical result does not connect unavoidable errors to the claimed absence of meaningful technological progress.
The deployment study does not measure whether hallucinations impose an ultimate reliability ceiling.
The claim supplies no task set or reliability threshold against which a broad causal conclusion can be settled.
